t: You're standing on Clapham Common, a big triangular park of 220 acres in south London. It began as common land for the parishes of Battersea and Clapham, and became parkland under the Metropolitan Commons Act of 1878. There are three ponds and a Victorian bandstand, and Georgian and Victorian mansions look over the grass towards Clapham Old Town. Several people were born here, among them Samuel Wilberforce, the bishop and third son of William Wilberforce, and the geographer Monica Cole, who went on to hold the Chair of Geography at Bedford College.
